title: Choose the visual world for TrustPass
question: The roll assigned the Bench Analyzer front panel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Bench Analyzer
options.lineage: lab oscilloscopes and pulse analyzers, the instruments that drive real qubits
options.thesis: TrustPass as a bench instrument: probe your circuit, pick the compiler as the signal source, read three channels.
options.viewport: The analyzer front panel fills the screen: qubit wires drawn as pulse traces on the graticule, three channel readouts below, a REJECT lamp lit because the saboteur slipped past two checks.
options.risk: Tips into skeuomorphic costume unless every knob and key is a real, working control.

raised.raise: The pipeline (lock, compile, unlock, verify, score) runs as one unbroken stage row with a chase light locked to the live run.
An acquisition ledger keeps every run you make, so the 5x3 detection matrix fills in from your own measurements.
Every setting is addressed in the URL, so a judge or the video can jump straight to the saboteur on FakeTorino.
Every readout carries a provenance tag: backend, transpiler seed and run number, so nothing on screen is an unsourced claim.
Numbers set as hairline lining figures on fixed tracks, the way an instrument prints measurements.

options.label: Chain of Custody
options.lineage: forensic evidence handling: sealed bags, tamper tape, custody logs
options.thesis: Your circuit as an exhibit: sealed before it leaves, logged at every hand-off, inspected when it comes back.
options.viewport: A sealed evidence bag holding the locked circuit, the custody log down the side, the returned exhibit stamped TAMPERED or CLEARED.
options.risk: Forensics is a familiar security costume, close to where most runs in this category land.

options.label: Clear-Line Album
options.thesis: The attack told as a four-tier album page: the circuit leaves, the compiler tampers, the checks investigate, the verdict lands.
options.viewport: A wide establishing panel of the circuit leaving your laptop, then tiers where each compiler's trick is missed by the naive test and caught by TrustPass.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and tells attack-then-defend most clearly; loses on audience identification with IBM engineers.
options.risk: Reads as a comic explainer rather than a working tool unless every panel is live.

options.label: Rhythm Machine Step Row
options.thesis: Five compilers as a step row, each check a lit key.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step row of compilers and checks under a chase light.
options.case: Same instrument family but judges don't read compilers as rhythm; loses both axes.
options.risk: Playful where the claim needs rigor.
options.kept: The one unbroken line with a chase light that always shows where now is.

options.label: Minihompy Room
options.thesis: Your circuit as a furnished room the compiler visits.
options.viewport: An isometric room with a guest ledger of who touched the circuit.
options.case: Charming but foreign to quantum engineers and blurs the verdict; loses both axes.
options.risk: Cute where trust is the subject.
options.kept: A persistent ledger: every visit leaves a record.

options.label: Teletext Mosaic
options.viewport: P100 index with the verdict as a mosaic block.
options.case: Blocky cells cannot draw circuits or evidence legibly; loses both axes.
options.kept: Every page addressed by number in the URL.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Circuits traded as shadows at a moonlit stall.
options.viewport: A lane of stalls, each circuit tagged with its origin ticket.
options.case: Poetic but obscures what was checked; loses both axes.
options.kept: Every item tagged with a ticket of origin.

options.label: Accretion Threshold
options.thesis: Your circuit crossing the compiler's event horizon.
options.viewport: A glowing disk with the verdict at the horizon.
options.case: Space spectacle is the category cliché and hides the checks; loses both axes.
options.kept: Hairline lining numerals on fixed tracks.

canonCard.label: The quantum dashboard standard
canonCard.thesis: What quantum hackathon demos ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar controls, a circuit diagram, metric cards and a results table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other quantum demo by design.
